subject: BioForge Private Deployment — scope, hardware checklist, and fallbacks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@bioforge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: BioForge private deployment signals and next info requests

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and the info we need to keep moving. High-level notes from our call: 

- BioForge preference: air-gapped on-prem deployment for Prod (compliance + IP).
- Possible staging/dev candidates: either Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Hosted API for non-sensitive workloads and burst capacity.
- Risk areas we discussed: offline upgrade windows, hardware refresh cadence, and remote support constraints for air-gapped nodes.

Action items (please confirm):
1) Share rack / BMC / networking inventory (U count, PDU type, top-of-rack switches, outbound egress controls).
2) Confirm whether on-site engineers can run preflight scripts and accept inbound console sessions for troubleshooting (we also offer an airgap-friendly USB image transfer flow).
3) Expected maintenance windows (recurring monthly, quarterly, or ad-hoc only).
4) Procurement timeline & who to loop for SOW/PO (procurement@bioforge.com?).

What we’ll send next: a tailored HW checklist for the air-gapped appliance, a suggested offline upgrade MOP, and an ops fallback diagram showing Hosted / Dedicated fallbacks for burst or critical incidents. I’ve attached the initial Redwood private HW spec draft.

If possible, please attach your rack inventory spreadsheet and flag any constraints by EOD Fri.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: BioForge private deployment signals and next info requests

Thanks Emily (and team) — reviewed the rack spreadsheet and sketched a minimal hardware checklist for an air-gapped Private deployment. Notes below are technical clarifications and a recommended baseline.

Minimal baseline (per appliance cluster):
- GPU nodes: 4x per cluster (NVIDIA A800 / H100 class recommended).
- CPU management node: 2x (for scheduler/control plane).
- NVMe local cache: 8TB usable per GPU node (for model artifacts + KV cache).
- RAM: 512GB per GPU node (workload dependent).
- Network: 25/100Gbps leaf with an internal management VLAN and an out-of-band management interface (BMC).
- Storage: Optional NFS for persistent logs; ensure RPO/RTO expectations.

Air-gap upgrade flow options:
A) Signed bundle hand-delivered on encrypted USB (customer-preferred for strict air-gap).
B) Sealed image with offline attestation and onsite application by BioForge ops.
C) Intermittent one-way data diode link to a hardened jump box for patch transfer (requires approval).

Fallbacks for burst: 
- Short-term: Redwood Hosted API (temporary keys scoped to burst projects) — fastest to enable but data-in-transit restrictions apply.
- Preferred: Dedicated reserved pool connected to a private VPC (keeps control plane isolated, predictable cost).

Next proposed steps from engineering:
1) We’ll create a short SOW draft for an on-site survey + 4-week pilot (attached is a SOW template).
2) If BioForge confirms allowed upgrade flows (A/B/C), we’ll map an MOP per choice and estimate labor/hours.
3) Lauren to build a preliminary commercial proposal (Dedicated vs Private CAPEX/ OPEX) and timeline.

I attached our hardware spec draft (redwood-private-hw-specs.pdf). Happy to jump on a 30-minute tech follow-up next week.

—Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-private-hw-specs.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@bioforge.com>, procurement@bioforge.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: two-track plan and site survey availability

Hi Emily / procurement team — following up with a practical two-track approach so you can move quickly without blocking Prod compliance evaluations: 

Track A — Quick pilot (4 weeks): Dedicated reserved capacity + private VPC for staging and early integration. Benefits: fast time-to-test, no hardware procurement, predictable monthly spend. Can be used to validate model behavior and integration with BioForge workflows.

Track B — Air-gapped on-prem pilot: full hardware provisioning and on-site survey, then a 6–8 week pilot with offline upgrade runbooks and local observability. This is the long-term target for Prod.

Please confirm which track you want to start in the next 2 weeks. For Track B we need: site-survey week preferred dates, PO contact, and which of the upgrade flows (A/B/C from Aditya’s note) you will allow.

Attached: SOW template and example upgrade MOP. Link to standard NDA/DocuSign: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123-nonprod

If procurement is ready we can issue a short commercial proposal by Wed (Lauren will own pricing). If you want, we can schedule the site-survey for week of 2026-11-02 — does that work?

Best,
—Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sow-template.docx

[Forwarded inline: short ops checklist and the recommended fallback diagram will follow in a separate email]
